To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the process of contaminated host cells is a nondegenerate subcritical branching process, (ii) the process of parasites is a nonde- generate subcritical martingale with stationary increments, (iii) the process of the number of parasites in a contaminated cell is a nondegener- ate martingale with a.s. positive jumps and stationary increments.
the process of contaminated host cells is a non-degenerate Kesten-Sti- gum process and that the process of parasites is a Kesten-Stigmum process.

(i) the process of contaminated host cells is asymptotically equivalent to a branching process in a random medium, (ii) the process of parasites is asymptotically a branching process in random medium, and (iii) the process of infected cells is asymptot- ically equivalent to a Galton-Watson branching process in random environment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of a general stochastic model for host-para- site coevolution.

the study of branching-within- branching processes, where the number of offspring of each individual in the first generation is random, and the offspring in the second generation are distributed according to a probability distribution depending on the number of offspring in the previous generation.
the study of the evolution of a parasite population within a host population.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the process of contaminated host cells converges to a non- degenerate limit if and only if the process of parasites is subcritical and the process of parasites has a positive probability to become extinct.
, for both processes, the limit is a nondegenerate random variable, which is positive with positive probability, if and only if certain integrability conditions hold.
, in the case of parasite survival, the process of contaminated hosts is asymptotically normal, whereas the process of parasites is asymptotic to a stable subordinator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the process of parasites is the most difficult one.
the process of contaminated hosts is asymptotically equivalent to the process of parasites, and the asymptotic behaviour of the former is determined by that of the latter.
the model is rich enough to exhibit both degenerate and nondegenerate limits, and that the degenerate case is not necessarily due to a lack of parasites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processes of parasites and contaminated cells can be viewed as two independent processes.
a general model for host-para- site co-evolution is amenable to a rigorous mathematical treatment.
the processes of contaminated hosts and of parasites have different asymptotic behavior.
